overall: Executive sessions for strategy on the superintendent's separation were proper, and no approval occurred in executive session; but the June 27 and July 2 notices were insufficiently detailed, a violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee improperly met in executive session to approve a settlement agreement with the former superintendent.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session to discuss strategy with respect to Dr. Chang’s severance agreement during both the June 27 and July 2 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee approved the settlement in executive session; the AG reviewed whether a contract was approved there.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Open Meeting Law does not permit a public body to approve a contract in executive session, see OML 2011-28, the Committee did not do so here.

allegations.summary: June 27 and July 2 executive session notices did not identify the non-union personnel the Committee would negotiate with, despite the superintendent's resignation being public.
allegations.key_passage: Here, both the June 27 and July 2 notices failed to identify the non-union personnel with whom the Committee would be negotiating.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
